definition_zh: 不情愿地；勉强地；不得已地
definition_en: in a way that shows one does not want to do something
core_image: 脚步磨着地面，一点一点往前移
scene: 图书馆要关门了，管理员第三次催人，男生才慢慢合上书。 He unwillingly left the reading room when the lights went out.
sceneCN: 这里 unwillingly 是「不情愿地」（第 1 个义项：不愿意却还是做了）；句意为灯灭时他才不得不离开阅览室。脚步磨着地面一点点往前移，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -ly 后得到的形容词，义为「不愿意的」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不愿；勉强」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「乐意地」
同源名词，义为「意愿；意志」

senses.title: Doing something without wanting to
senses.definition: doing what is asked while making clear that one does not want to
senses.definitionCN: 照要求去做，同时表明自己并不愿意
senses.example: She unwillingly agreed to sing at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 她勉强答应在聚会上唱歌。
senses.why: The adverb simply carries the idea of an absent will onto the verb: the action runs against the wish.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把「意愿缺席」直接带到动词上：动作与心愿背道而驰。

senses.title: Parting with something with regret
senses.definition: giving something up while still wanting to keep it
senses.definitionCN: 把东西交出去，心里却还想留着
senses.example: He unwillingly handed the keys to the new owner.
senses.exampleCN: 他不情愿地把钥匙交给新主人。
senses.why: The adverb turns the absent will toward an object, and what one still wants to keep leaves the hand slowly.
senses.whyCN: 副词把缺席的意愿指向某个对象，于是还想留着的东西就这么慢慢离开了手。

senses.title: Accepting a fact one would rather deny
senses.definition: admitting something only because the evidence leaves no choice
senses.definitionCN: 只因证据不容否认才承认某事
senses.example: She unwillingly admitted that the plan had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 她勉强承认这个计划失败了。
senses.why: Resistance to the act becomes resistance to the truth, and admission is the act forced by evidence.
senses.whyCN: 对动作的抵触变成对事实的抵触，而承认正是被证据逼出来的动作。

senses.title: Obeying an order without agreement
senses.definition: following an order while disagreeing with it
senses.definitionCN: 在不认同的情况下照命令行事
senses.example: The clerk unwillingly followed the new rule.
senses.exampleCN: 店员不得已照新规定办事。
senses.why: A will that is absent does not stop the feet; obedience without agreement is what remains.
senses.whyCN: 意愿缺席并不能让脚停下来，剩下就是「照做却不同意」。

senses.title: Getting out of bed or leaving a place
senses.definition: moving slowly because one has no wish to go
senses.definitionCN: 因为不想去而动作迟缓
senses.example: They unwillingly got up when the alarm rang again.
senses.exampleCN: 闹钟又响时，他们才磨磨蹭蹭地起床。
senses.why: When no wish moves the body, the body moves slowly, so the adverb also names dragging feet.
senses.whyCN: 没有意愿推动身体，身体就走得慢，于是这个副词也用来形容拖沓的脚步。

intro.en: A negative prefix, the old noun for will, a participle ending, and the adverb ending stack in a clear line.
intro.cn: 否定前缀、古老的「意愿」名词、分词词尾与副词词尾依次清晰地叠加。

items.en: Willa meant wish, and un- was already used to deny a quality.
items.cn: willa 意为「愿望」，un- 当时已用于否定某种性质。

items.en: Willing is formed from will, and the adverb adds -ly to make willingly.
items.cn: willing 由 will 构成，副词再加 -ly 得到 willingly。

items.en: Unwilling follows the same pattern with the negative prefix in front.
items.cn: unwilling 以同样的方式构成，只是前面加了否定前缀。

items.en: Unwillingly appears as the regular adverb in written usage from the modern period.
items.cn: unwillingly 作为规则副词在现代时期的书面语中出现。

items.en: It is common with verbs of agreeing, accepting, and parting.
items.cn: 它常与「同意、接受、割舍」一类的动词连用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers adverbs built on will, and the near-meaning group collects adverbs of reluctance.
note.cn: 形近组汇集建在 will 上的副词，近义组汇集表示不情愿的副词。

normalIntro.en: Four familiar pieces stack in a row: not, will, the participle ending, and the adverb ending.
normalIntro.cn: 四个熟悉的部分依次叠起：否定、意愿、分词词尾与副词词尾。

normal.en: Break it as un- plus willing plus -ly, and nothing is left unexplained.
normal.cn: 拆成 un- 加 willing 加 -ly，就没有解释不了的部分。

normal.en: It usually sits after the verb or at the front of the clause.
normal.cn: 它通常放在动词后或从句前部。

normal.en: Agree unwillingly and leave unwillingly are the two solid collocations.
normal.cn: agree unwillingly 与 leave unwillingly 是两个扎实的搭配。

normal.en: Reluctantly is close but stresses hesitation, not will.
normal.cn: reluctantly 意思相近，但强调的是迟疑而非意愿。

normal.en: The adjective form is the adjective to learn first.
normal.cn: 先记住形容词形式，副词只是加 -ly。

abstract.en: Hear shoes scraping slowly on a wooden floor.
abstract.cn: 听鞋子在木地板上磨蹭的声音。

abstract.en: See keys dropped into another palm one by one.
abstract.cn: 看见钥匙一把一把落进别人的掌心。

abstract.en: Watch a hand push a door open and hold it back.
abstract.cn: 看一只手把门推开，又往回带。

examples.en: He unwillingly signed the form and pushed it back across the desk.
examples.cn: 他不情愿地签了表，又从桌上推了回去。

examples.en: The children unwillingly turned off the game when dinner was called.
examples.cn: 听到喊吃饭，孩子们不情愿地关掉了游戏。

examples.en: She unwillingly admitted that the plan had failed.
examples.cn: 她勉强承认这个计划失败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不灵了」——心里一直念着俺不灵了，手上的活儿就做得磨磨蹭蹭。

root: 英语本土构词：un-（不）+ will（意愿）+ -ing（分词词尾）+ -ly（副词词尾），will 源自古代英语 willa / willan

sensesIntro.en: One adverb for acting against the wish covers consent, parting, admission, obedience, and slow departure.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示「违背心愿而做」的副词，覆盖答应、割舍、承认、服从与磨蹭离开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shoes scraping along the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：鞋底在地上磨着走。

branches.en: The consent branch: a yes that sounds like a sigh.
branches.cn: 答应分支：一声答应带着叹息。

branches.en: The parting branch: something leaves the hand slowly.
branches.cn: 割舍分支：东西慢慢离开手心。

branches.en: The admission branch: a truth spoken under pressure.
branches.cn: 承认分支：被逼出来的实话。

branches.en: The obedience branch: an order followed with no agreement.
branches.cn: 服众分支：照着命令做却不认同。

branches.en: The departure branch: leaving one step at a time.
branches.cn: 离开分支：一步一停地走。

intro.en: Four common pieces in a row, each still clear in the meaning.
intro.cn: 四个常见部件依次排列，各自的含义仍然清楚。

latinIntro.en: The base is Germanic; in Latin the matching adverb would be built on invitus, unwilling.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属日耳曼语；拉丁语中对应的副词要建在 invitus（不情愿的）上。

items.example: He had no will to fight.

definition_zh: 汽车，机动车；（作定语）汽车的
definition_en: a road vehicle with an engine, especially a car, or used before a noun to mean relating to cars
core_image: 一辆四轮车自己发动，载着人离开门口
scene: 老照片里，街上的马车旁边第一次停了一辆不用马拉的车。 The automobile changed how cities grew.
sceneCN: 这里 automobile 是「汽车」（第 1 个义项：四轮机动车）；句意是汽车改变了城市扩张的方式。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：汽车的；机动车的

senses.title: Engine-powered road car
senses.definition: a road vehicle with its own engine, especially a passenger car
senses.definitionCN: 自带发动机的道路车辆，尤指载客汽车
senses.example: The automobile changed how cities grew.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车改变了城市扩张的方式。
senses.why: The word was coined when engineers needed a formal name for a carriage that moves itself, so it names the machine rather than the everyday car.
senses.whyCN: 工程师需要为「自己能走的马车」取一个正式名字，于是造出这个词，所以它指的是机器本身，而不是日常口语里的车。

senses.title: Car as a modifier
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean of or relating to cars
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示与汽车有关的
senses.example: He works in the automobile industry.
senses.exampleCN: 他在汽车行业工作。
senses.why: In compounds the noun loses its plural and works like an adjective, naming a whole field such as industry, age or accident.
senses.whyCN: 在复合词里这个名词不用复数，起形容词作用，用来命名整个领域，如工业、时代或事故。

intro.en: Automobile is a French-made word meaning self-moving.
intro.cn: automobile 是法语造的，意思是「自己能动的」。

items.en: autos meant 'self'.
items.cn: autos 意为「自己」。

items.en: mobile came from Latin mobilis, 'able to move'.
items.cn: mobile 来自拉丁语 mobilis，意为「能移动的」。

items.en: automobile was coined for a self-moving vehicle.
items.cn: automobile 被造出来指自行移动的车辆。

items.en: English adopted it as the formal word for a motor car.
items.cn: 英语在 1897 年采用它作为汽车的正式说法。

items.en: Everyday speech shortened it to auto and car.
items.cn: 日常口语把它缩短成 auto 与 car。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the auto- prefix; the near-meaning group gives words for road vehicles.
note.cn: 形近组共享 auto- 前缀；近义组是表示道路车辆的词。

entries.definition: a road vehicle for a few passengers
a car, in older British use

normalIntro.en: Automobile is a description turned into a name: self plus moving.
normalIntro.cn: automobile 是把一个描述变成了名字：自己加移动。

normal.en: Break it into auto, self, and mobile, moving.
normal.cn: 拆成 auto「自己」和 mobile「可移动的」。

normal.en: It is the formal word; car is the everyday one.
normal.cn: 它是正式说法，car 是日常说法。

normal.en: Before another noun it keeps the singular: automobile industry.
normal.cn: 放在另一名词前时用单数：automobile industry。

normal.en: The short form auto belongs to American English.
normal.cn: 缩略形式 auto 属于美式英语。

normal.en: Automotive is the adjective used for the whole industry.
normal.cn: automotive 是用于整个行业的形容词。

abstract.en: See a carriage roll forward with no horse in front.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆马车向前走，前面却没有马。

abstract.en: See a factory line of identical bodies in a row.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂流水线上一排一模一样的车身。

abstract.en: See an old photo of a street half horse, half engine.
abstract.cn: 想象一张老照片，街上半是马车，半是汽车。

examples.en: The automobile changed how cities grew.
examples.cn: 汽车改变了城市扩张的方式。

examples.en: He works in the automobile industry.
examples.cn: 他在汽车行业工作。

examples.en: The museum keeps an early automobile in working order.
examples.cn: 博物馆保存着一辆仍能开动的早期汽车。

dict_mnemonic.text: auto（自己）加 mobile（能动的）：不用马拉、自己会走的车，就是 automobile；放到名词前就表示「汽车的」。

root: 由希腊语 autos「自己」与拉丁语 mobilis「能移动的」组合，经法语 automobile 进入英语；十九世纪末用来命名不用马拉的机动车，后来日常口语简化为 auto 与 car。

sensesIntro.en: The name describes the machine, and the same word can label the whole industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名字描述机器本身，同一个词也能标注整个行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carriage that moves with no horse.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆不用马拉却自己在走的马车。

branches.en: an early automobile
branches.cn: 早期汽车

branches.en: an electric automobile
branches.cn: 电动汽车

branches.en: the automobile industry
branches.cn: 汽车工业

branches.en: the automobile age
branches.cn: 汽车时代

branches.en: an automobile accident
branches.cn: 汽车事故

intro.en: The prefix auto-, 'self', joins mobile, 'moving', to make automobile.
intro.cn: 前缀 auto-「自己」加 mobile「可移动的」，构成 automobile。

latinIntro.en: The moving half is Latin mobilis; the self half is Greek autos.
latinIntro.cn: 「移动」那一半来自拉丁语 mobilis，「自己」那一半来自希腊语 autos。

definition_zh: 肋骨；排骨；肋状结构
definition_en: one of the curved bones around the chest
core_image: X 光片上，一排弯弯的骨线围住胸腔
scene: 他从自行车上摔下来，断了一根肋骨。 He fell off his bicycle and broke a rib.
sceneCN: 这里 rib 是「肋骨」（第 1 个义项：围住胸腔的弯骨）；句意：他从自行车上摔下来，断了一根肋骨。

senses.title: Chest bone
senses.definition: one of the curved bones around the chest
senses.definitionCN: 围住胸腔的弯骨之一
senses.example: She cracked a rib while coughing.
senses.exampleCN: 她咳嗽时把肋骨咳裂了。
senses.why: The word has long named the curved bones of the chest.
senses.whyCN: 这个词长期指胸腔的弯骨。

senses.title: Meat cut
senses.definition: a piece of meat with a rib bone
senses.definitionCN: 带肋骨的肉块
senses.example: We had ribs for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 我们晚餐吃了排骨。
senses.why: The bone gives its name to the meat around it.
senses.whyCN: 骨头把自己的名字给了周围的肉。

senses.title: Supporting strip
senses.definition: a curved strip that supports a structure
senses.definitionCN: 支撑结构的弯曲条状物
senses.example: The ribs of the umbrella are made of steel.
senses.exampleCN: 伞骨是钢制的。
senses.why: Anything rib-like can borrow the same shape word.
senses.whyCN: 任何像肋骨的形状都能借用这个词。

intro.en: Rib is an old English word, ribb, with a Germanic past.
intro.cn: rib 是古英语词 ribb，有着日耳曼语渊源。

items.en: Ribb names a bone of the chest.
items.cn: ribb 指胸腔的骨头。

items.en: The word is common to Germanic languages.
items.cn: 这个词在日耳曼语族中普遍存在。

items.en: Rib keeps the same shape and meaning.
items.cn: rib 保留了相同的形态和含义。

items.en: It also names a cut of meat.
items.cn: 它也指一种肉块。

items.en: It describes curved supports as well.
items.cn: 它还描述弯曲的支撑结构。

note.en: Rib is a bone; a strip is any long narrow piece.
note.cn: rib 是骨头；strip 泛指任何长条。

entries.definition: a hard part of the body

normalIntro.en: Ribs are the curved bars that guard the heart.
normalIntro.cn: rib 是守护心脏的弯曲栅栏。

normal.en: A rib cage protects the lungs.
normal.cn: 胸廓保护肺。

normal.en: Spare ribs are a popular dish.
normal.cn: 排骨是一道受欢迎的菜。

normal.en: The umbrella has steel ribs.
normal.cn: 这把伞有钢制伞骨。

normal.en: He broke a rib playing football.
normal.cn: 他踢足球时断了一根肋骨。

normal.en: Compare bone: every rib is a bone, but not every bone is a rib.
normal.cn: 对比 bone：每根肋骨都是骨头，但不是每根骨头都是肋骨。

abstract.en: Picture curved bars around a small room.
abstract.cn: 想象围住小房间的弯曲栅栏。

abstract.en: Imagine a basket woven from long thin strips.
abstract.cn: 想象一只用细长条编成的篮子。

abstract.en: Think of a hug that holds without touching.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不触碰却托住你的怀抱。

examples.en: The X-ray showed a broken rib.
examples.cn: X 光片上显示一根肋骨骨折。

examples.en: She cooked spare ribs for the family.
examples.cn: 她为家人做了排骨。

examples.en: The tent is held open by thin ribs.
examples.cn: 帐篷靠细长的肋杆撑开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rib」三个字母短促有力——像一根弯曲的肋骨，也像敲两下的短音。

root: 古英语 ribb（肋）→ 中古英语 rib → 现代英语 rib，核心义「胸腔的弯骨及其相似结构」。

sensesIntro.en: Rib first names the chest bone, then the meat around it, and finally any curved supporting strip.
sensesIntro.cn: rib 先指胸腔的骨头，再指其周围的肉，最后指任何弯曲的支撑条。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: curved bone lines around a chest on an X-ray.
core.cn: 核心意象：X 光片上围住胸腔的弯骨线条。

branches.en: The chest bone is the core sense.
branches.cn: 胸腔的骨头是核心含义。

branches.en: The meat around the bone takes the name.
branches.cn: 骨边的肉沿用了这个名字。

branches.en: Curved supports are rib-like.
branches.cn: 弯曲的支撑物像肋骨。

branches.en: Bone and meat are named together.
branches.cn: 骨头与肉一起被命名。

branches.en: Both the body and objects use the curved shape.
branches.cn: 身体与器物都用这种弯曲形状。

intro.en: Rib is a short Old English word with a Germanic past.
intro.cn: rib 是一个简短的古英语词，有日耳曼语渊源。

latinIntro.en: It has no Latin root; the word comes from Old English ribb.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，来自古英语 ribb。

items.example: Ribb is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: ribb 是现存最古老的形式。
ribbed 描述有条纹的表面。

items.example: Rib cage names the whole frame.

definition_zh: 药物；药剂；用药；药物治疗
definition_en: a drug used to treat a disease or relieve symptoms, and also the act or course of taking such drugs
core_image: 床头柜上一只分格药盒，每一格放着不同颜色的小药片，旁边是一杯水和一张服药时间表
scene: 清晨的厨房里，老人把一周的药片按格子分好，水杯边压着一张写着时间的纸条。 The nurse asked him whether he was still taking his medication for blood pressure.
sceneCN: 这里是「用药、服药」（第 2 个义项：服用药物的过程）；句意是护士问他是否仍在服用降压药。图中可辨识物件：分格药盒、水杯、时间表。

pos.zh: 药物；药剂；用药；药物治疗

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 medic 加 -ate 构成，义为「给……用药；治疗」
由同一词干加 -al 构成，义为「医学的；医疗的」
由同一词干加 -ment 构成，义为「药物；药剂」
由 medicate 加 -ed 构成，义为「含药物的；经药物处理的」
由 medical 加 -ly 构成，义为「医学上；从医学角度」

senses.title: A drug used to treat illness
senses.definition: a substance, usually a drug, taken to treat a disease or to relieve its symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 为治疗疾病或缓解症状而服用的物质，通常是药物
senses.example: The doctor changed her medication because the first one caused nausea.
senses.exampleCN: 医生给她换了药，因为第一种药让她恶心。
senses.why: Latin medicatio began as the act of healing, and the thing taken to heal naturally took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 medicatio 起初指「治疗」这一行为，用来治病的那个东西也自然沿用了同一个名字。

senses.title: The act or course of taking medicine
senses.definition: the practice or course of taking prescribed drugs over time, especially for a long-term condition
senses.definitionCN: 长期按医嘱服用药物的做法或疗程，尤指针对慢性病
senses.example: His medication lasted six months, with a check-up every four weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 他的疗程持续六个月，每四周复查一次。
senses.why: If the word can name the drug, it can also name the whole routine built around it, including the timing and the checks.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指药物本身，也就能指围绕药物建立的一整套流程，包括服药时间与复查。

senses.title: The giving of drugs as treatment
senses.definition: the administering of drugs to a patient, a technical sense used in medical writing
senses.definitionCN: 向病人施用药物的行为，是医学写作中的技术性用法
senses.example: Nurses record the time of every medication in the ward.
senses.exampleCN: 护士记录病房里每一次给药的时间。
senses.why: The Latin noun was abstract, naming the act of healing, so this technical branch keeps the original act rather than the pill.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词本是抽象名词，指治疗的行为，因此这一技术性分支保留的是动作本身，而不是药片。

intro.en: Medication comes from Latin words about healing, and its abstract sense of treatment slowly shifted toward the drugs themselves.
intro.cn: medication 来自拉丁语中与医治有关的词，其「治疗」的抽象义逐渐转向药物本身。

items.en: Mederi meant to heal or to cure, and it is the oldest layer behind the whole word family.
items.cn: mederi 意为医治、治愈，是整个词族最古老的一层。

items.en: Medicus named the physician, the person who heals, and the adjective medicus meant healing.
items.cn: medicus 指医生，也就是治病的人，作形容词时意为「治疗的」。

items.en: Medicatio named the act of treating and the treatment itself, abstract rather than a concrete object.
items.cn: medicatio 指治疗的行为与疗程，是抽象说法，而非具体器物。

items.en: French médication kept the abstract sense of treatment and passed it into English medical prose.
items.cn: 法语 médication 保留「治疗」这一抽象义，并把它传入英语医学文章。

items.en: Modern English shifted medication toward the drugs themselves, especially long-term prescribed drugs.
items.cn: 现代英语把 medication 的重心转向药物本身，尤指长期按医嘱服用的药。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the healing word family; the near-meaning group collects the things taken and the treatments given.
note.cn: 形近组收表示医治的词族；近义组收服用的药物与施行的疗法。

entries.definition: The broader word for drugs and for the healing art, with no focus on a course of treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽泛的词，既指药也指医学，不强调疗程。

entries.definition: Relating to the treatment of illness rather than to a particular drug.
entries.definitionCN: 与疾病治疗有关，而非指某种具体药物。

entries.definition: To give a person a drug as part of treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 作为治疗的一部分给某人用药。

entries.definition: A formal word for a healing substance or remedy.
A substance that changes how the body works, used as medicine or abused.
entries.definitionCN: 改变身体运作方式的物质，可作药物，也可被滥用。

entries.definition: Something that cures or relieves a problem, often a treatment rather than a pill.
entries.definitionCN: 能治愈或缓解问题的东西，常指疗法而非药片。

entries.definition: A small round piece of medicine that is swallowed.
A doctor's written order for a drug, or the drug so ordered.
entries.definitionCN: 医生开具的药方，或按方配的药。

entries.definition: The care given to cure an illness, which may or may not involve drugs.
entries.definitionCN: 为治愈疾病而给予的照护，未必涉及药物。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin stem for healing; its family keeps the doctor, the act of treating and the substances used.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示医治的拉丁词干上，同族词反复出现医生、治疗行为与所用之物。

normal.en: Medicus in Latin is the doctor, and medication is what that doctor sets in motion.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 medicus 是医生，medication 就是这位医生启动的那套治疗。

normal.en: The -ation ending marks an action, so medication first meant the act of treating.
normal.cn: -ation 词尾标记行为，所以 medication 起初指治疗这件事。

normal.en: Medicate is the verb: to put a patient on a drug.
normal.cn: medicate 是动词，意为给病人用药。

normal.en: Medical adds -al and describes anything belonging to healing.
normal.cn: medical 加 -al，描述属于医疗的一切。

normal.en: Medicament is the older noun for the substance itself, now mostly formal.
normal.cn: medicament 是较早指药物本身的名称，现在多为正式用法。

abstract.en: A word for healing first named the act and then the pill, which shows how easily a process turns into an object.
abstract.cn: 一个表示医治的词先指行为、后指药片，这说明过程多么容易变成物件。

abstract.en: Taking medication is a routine, not a single moment, and the word holds both the substance and the schedule.
abstract.cn: 服药是一套流程而非一个瞬间，这个词同时装下了药物与时间表。

abstract.en: The same stem gives the doctor, the drug and the act, three sides of one attempt to make a body well again.
abstract.cn: 同一词干给出医生、药物与行为，是让身体康复这一尝试的三个侧面。

examples.en: She keeps her medication in a locked cabinet.
examples.cn: 她把药物锁在柜子里。

examples.en: Missing a dose of medication can be dangerous for heart patients.
examples.cn: 漏服一次药对心脏病人可能很危险。

examples.en: The clinic offers free medication for long-term patients.
examples.cn: 诊所为长期病人提供免费药物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦迪凯申」——像药瓶上的品牌名；记住 medication 是药物。

root: 拉丁语 mederi（医治）派生出 medicus（医生）与 medicatio（治疗），经法语进入英语；同族词多与医疗、用药有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is healing through drugs; the senses separate into the substance, the course of taking it and the clinical act of giving it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是借药物医治；义项分为药物本身、服药疗程与临床给药这一行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weekly pill organiser on a bedside table, each compartment holding pills of a different colour, with a glass of water and a timetable beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：床头柜上一只分格药盒，每一格放着不同颜色的小药片，旁边是一杯水与一张服药时间表。

branches.en: a brown bottle whose label lists a dose
branches.cn: 标签上写着剂量的棕色药瓶

branches.en: a weekly tray with seven rows of pills
branches.cn: 分成七排药片的周用药盒

branches.en: a calendar with a tick beside every evening
branches.cn: 每晚旁边都打了勾的日历

branches.en: a nurse writing the hour on a ward chart
branches.cn: 护士在病房记录表上写下时间

branches.en: a trolley of small cups carried down a corridor
branches.cn: 沿走廊推过的一车小药杯

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin verb of healing, its doctor noun, the abstract noun of treatment, and English endings that build verbs and adjectives.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示医治的拉丁动词、指医生的名词、表示治疗的抽象名词，以及构成动词与形容词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 有光泽的；闪亮的；崭新的；光鲜的
definition_en: reflecting light smoothly, full of small bright points, looking new, or seeming perfect
core_image: 一双擦得发亮的新皮鞋，映出窗外的光
scene: 他的鞋旧了，但依然闪亮。 His shoes were old but still shiny.
sceneCN: 这里 shiny 是「闪亮的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的鞋旧了，但依然闪亮。

senses.title: Glossy
senses.definition: reflecting light smoothly
senses.definitionCN: 平滑地反射光
senses.example: The table had a shiny surface.
senses.exampleCN: 桌面有光泽。
senses.why: This is the core sense from shine plus -y.
senses.whyCN: 这是 shine 加 -y 的核心义项。

senses.title: Bright
senses.definition: full of small points of light
senses.definitionCN: 布满细小光点
senses.example: The tree was covered in shiny lights.
senses.exampleCN: 树上挂满了闪亮的小灯。
senses.why: Small reflections look like sparkles.
senses.whyCN: 细小的反光看起来像闪烁。

senses.title: New-looking
senses.definition: looking new and unused
senses.definitionCN: 看起来新而未用过
senses.example: He drove a shiny new car.
senses.exampleCN: 他开着一辆崭新的车。
senses.why: New things are often polished.
senses.whyCN: 新东西通常被擦得发亮。

senses.title: Perfect-seeming
senses.definition: seeming perfect but perhaps not real
senses.definitionCN: 看似完美但也许不真实
senses.example: The shiny image hid a weak product.
senses.exampleCN: 光鲜的形象掩盖了薄弱的产品。
senses.why: Gloss can cover flaws.
senses.whyCN: 光泽可以遮盖瑕疵。

intro.en: Shiny is the adjective built from shine with the ending -y.
intro.cn: shiny 是由 shine 加后缀 -y 构成的形容词。

items.en: Scinan is the verb behind shiny.
items.cn: scinan 是 shiny 背后的动词。

items.en: Shiny formed with -y from shine.
items.cn: shiny 由 shine 加 -y 形成。

items.en: Shiny described polished metals and smooth cloth.
items.cn: shiny 形容擦亮的金属与光滑的布。

items.en: Shiny extended to new or impressive things.
items.cn: shiny 扩展到崭新或引人注目的东西。

items.en: Shiny new became a common phrase.
items.cn: shiny new 成为常用短语。

note.en: Shiny is compared with similar-looking words and with words for gloss.
note.cn: 把 shiny 与形近词以及表示光泽的词作比较。

entries.definition: the front of the lower leg
a Scottish stick and ball game
smooth and shiny on the surface

normalIntro.en: Shiny describes any surface that throws light back at you.
normalIntro.cn: shiny 形容任何把光反射回来的表面。

normal.en: Her hair is shiny.
normal.cn: 她的头发有光泽。

normal.en: The car is shiny and new.
normal.cn: 这辆车崭新发亮。

normal.en: The floor looks shiny after waxing.
normal.cn: 打蜡后地板看起来很亮。

normal.en: He wore shiny black shoes.
normal.cn: 他穿着闪亮的黑皮鞋。

normal.en: The coin was small but shiny.
normal.cn: 那枚硬币很小但很亮。

abstract.en: A shiny coat can hide an old engine.
abstract.cn: 光亮的车漆可能藏着旧发动机。

abstract.en: Light loves a smooth surface.
abstract.cn: 光偏爱光滑的表面。

abstract.en: New things look shiny before they are tested.
abstract.cn: 新东西在被检验之前都显得光鲜。

examples.en: The table had a shiny surface.
examples.cn: 桌面有光泽。

examples.en: He drove a shiny new car.
examples.cn: 他开着一辆崭新的车。

examples.en: The shiny image hid a weak product.
examples.cn: 光鲜的形象掩盖了薄弱的产品。

dict_mnemonic.text: shiny 就是 shine 加 -y：会反光的、擦得亮的，也可指看起来崭新的东西。

root: 由古英语 scinan（发光）加形容词后缀 -y 构成，核心义「反光的」。

sensesIntro.en: Shiny means glossy, bright, looking new, or seeming perfect.
sensesIntro.cn: shiny 意为有光泽的、闪亮的、崭新的或光鲜的。

core.en: A surface that sends light back to the eye.
core.cn: 把光反射回眼睛的表面。

branches.en: A smooth table reflects light.
branches.cn: 光滑的桌面反射光。

branches.en: Small lights sparkle on the tree.
branches.cn: 小灯在树上闪烁。

branches.en: A new car looks polished.
branches.cn: 新车看起来像被擦亮过。

branches.en: A glossy image can hide flaws.
branches.cn: 光鲜的形象可能掩盖瑕疵。

branches.en: Reflection and newness often appear together.
branches.cn: 反光与崭新常常同时出现。

intro.en: Shiny forms a family of gloss and light words.
intro.cn: shiny 形成一个表示光泽与光亮的词族。

latinIntro.en: Shiny has no Latin ancestor; Latin nitidus, shining, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shiny 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 nitidus（闪亮的）只是语义对应词。

items.example: This coin is shinier than that one.
The metal shines in the sun.
A shining coin lay on the path.
items.exampleCN: 一枚闪亮的硬币躺在路上。

definition_zh: 截止期限；最后期限
definition_en: the latest time by which something must be finished
core_image: 墙上的钟快指到午夜，桌上还堆着没写完的稿子
scene: 编辑在日历上圈出周五，说那天必须交稿。 The deadline is Friday at noon.
sceneCN: 这里 deadline 指「截止期限」（第 1 个义项：必须完成某事的最晚时间）；句意是截止时间是周五中午。

senses.title: The last moment allowed
senses.definition: the fixed time after which work is no longer accepted
senses.definitionCN: 过了这个时间，工作就不再被接受
senses.example: The deadline is Friday at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 截止时间是周五中午。
senses.why: A line drawn across time works like a line drawn on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 在时间上画的一条线，和在地上画的一条线一样管用。

senses.title: A line one must not cross
senses.definition: the original sense: a boundary in a prison camp that guards would shoot across
senses.definitionCN: 最初的义项：战俘营里一道越过去就会被开枪射击的界线
senses.example: The old prison deadline was marked with white stones.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧战俘营的界线是用白石标出的。
senses.why: The word began as a line you crossed only once, and time borrowed its force.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是一条只能越一次的线，时间借走了它的力量。

intro.en: Deadline first named a real line on the ground in an American prison camp during the civil war.
intro.cn: deadline 最初指美国内战时期战俘营地上一条真实的界线。

items.en: A deadline was a line past which prisoners would be shot.
items.cn: deadline 指战俘越过就会被射杀的界线。

items.en: Printers used the word for a line of type beyond the page.
items.cn: 印刷工用它指超出页面的一道字行。

items.en: Newspapers used deadline for the hour a story had to be in.
items.cn: 报社用它指稿件必须交到的钟点。

items.en: The word spread from newsrooms into every kind of work.
items.cn: 这个词从新闻编辑室扩散到各行各业。

items.en: A deadline is now any moment that ends the time allowed.
items.cn: 如今 deadline 指任何结束允许时间的时刻。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dead- or -line shape, and the meaning group names other ends of time.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dead- 或 -line 的词形，近义组则列出时间的其他终点。

entries.definitionCN: 不再活着或不再运转的

entries.definition: a state where neither side can move
entries.definitionCN: 双方都无法前进的僵局

entries.definition: the point at which something stops being allowed
entries.definitionCN: 某事不再被允许的那个点

entries.definition: the greatest amount or point permitted
entries.definitionCN: 被允许的最大量或最远点

entries.definition: the day on which something must be handed in
entries.definitionCN: 必须交上某物的那一天

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line on prison ground and end with a clock that refuses to wait.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从战俘营地上的一条线开始，落到一只不肯等人的钟。

normal.en: A deadline is a wall built out of minutes.
normal.cn: 截止期，是用分钟砌起来的一堵墙。

normal.en: The word once meant a line you could not walk past.
normal.cn: 这个词从前指一条不能走过去的线。

normal.en: Work stretches until a deadline gives it a shape.
normal.cn: 工作一直拖着，直到截止期给它一个形状。

normal.en: A missed deadline is louder than a late excuse.
normal.cn: 错过的截止期，比迟到的解释更响。

normal.en: The clock does not move faster; only the room does.
normal.cn: 钟没有走快，是屋里的人变快了。

abstract.en: Picture a clock on a wall and a page still blank.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一只钟，桌上还是一张白纸。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a folder across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把文件夹推过柜台。

abstract.en: Picture white stones laid in a straight line on bare ground.
abstract.cn: 想象空地上用白石摆出的一条直线。

examples.en: The deadline is Friday at noon.
examples.cn: 截止时间是周五中午。

examples.en: They worked all night to meet the deadline.
examples.cn: 为了赶上截止期，他们干了一整夜。

examples.en: The editor agreed to extend the deadline by a week.
examples.cn: 编辑同意把截止期延长一周。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deadline 记成「死线」：dead 是死，line 是线，一条过了就完了的线，就是截止期。

root: 由 dead（死的）与 line（线）复合而成，十九世纪六十年代美国战俘营里指越界即被射杀的界线；印刷业与报社先后借用，二十世纪起泛指一切必须完成工作的最后时刻。

sensesIntro.en: From a line on the ground you must not cross, to a line on the clock you must not pass.
sensesIntro.cn: 从地上不能越过的线，到钟上不能越过的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn across time with a clock behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：横在时间上的一条线，身后是一只钟。

branches.en: The first sense is the modern one: the last accepted moment.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是现代义：最后被接受的那一刻。

branches.en: The second is the literal line that gave the word its force.
branches.cn: 第二个是给这个词以力量的那条真实的线。

branches.en: Both senses share one rule: past this point, there is no return.
branches.cn: 两个义项共用一条规矩：过了这点，就回不去了。

branches.en: The prison line became a metaphor the moment offices needed one.
branches.cn: 办公室一需要比喻，战俘营的那条线就变成了比喻。

branches.en: A deadline is frightening because it remembers being deadly.
branches.cn: 截止期之所以吓人，是因为它记得自己曾经致命。

intro.en: Deadline is a compound, so its family is built by pairing it with the verbs and nouns of work.
intro.cn: deadline 是复合词，它的一族靠与工作相关的动词和名词搭配而成。

latinIntro.en: The two halves are native English: dead from Old English dēad, line from Latin linea through French.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都算英语本族：dead 出自古英语 dēad，line 则经法语来自拉丁语 linea。

items.meaning: to fail to finish in time
items.example: He missed the deadline by a day.

items.meaning: a deadline that leaves little time
items.example: She works well under a tight deadline.
items.exampleCN: 期限紧迫时她反而干得好。

items.meaning: the stress caused by a deadline
items.example: Deadline pressure kept him at his desk.
items.exampleCN: 截止期的压力把他按在桌前。

definition_zh: 跳水；潜水；猛冲；暴跌
definition_en: to jump head first into water, to move down quickly, or to fall sharply in value
core_image: 一个人站在池边，脚尖离水面只有一线，身体向前折下
scene: 池边安静了一秒，他弯下身子。 She dived into the cold water without a sound.
sceneCN: 这里 dive 指「跳水」（第 1 个义项：头朝下跃入水中）；句意是她无声地跃入冷水。

senses.title: To go head first into water
senses.definition: to jump into water with your head and arms going first
senses.definitionCN: 头和手臂先入水地跳进水里
senses.example: He dived from the top board.
senses.exampleCN: 他从最高的跳板跳下去。
senses.why: The body makes one clean line before it meets the water.
senses.whyCN: 身体先拉成一条干净的线，才碰到水面。

senses.title: To move down fast
senses.definition: to move quickly downwards or into something
senses.definitionCN: 快速向下移动或扎进某处
senses.example: The plane dived towards the runway.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机朝跑道俯冲。
senses.why: Speed turns a fall into a decision.
senses.whyCN: 有了速度，坠落也像是一个决定。

senses.title: A sharp fall in value
senses.definition: a sudden large drop in prices or numbers
senses.definitionCN: 价格或数字突然大幅下跌
senses.example: Shares took a dive after the news.
senses.exampleCN: 消息出来后股价大跌。
senses.why: A market that climbs slowly can still leave in one jump.
senses.whyCN: 慢慢爬上去的行情，也可能一跳就走。

intro.en: Dive goes back to Old English dyfan, to dip or sink, a word shared with deep.
intro.cn: dive 可追到古英语 dyfan（浸、沉），与 deep 同源。

items.en: Dyfan meant to dip something into liquid.
items.cn: dyfan 指把东西浸进液体。

items.en: A diver was already a man who went under water.
items.cn: 古英语里已有指下水之人的说法。

items.en: The verb settled as dive with a long i sound.
items.cn: 中古英语时动词固定为 dive，元音拉长。

items.en: Sporting dives from boards became a public show.
items.cn: 从跳板跳水成了公开表演。

items.en: The word spread to planes, shares and sudden rushes.
items.cn: 后来扩展到飞机、股价与突然的冲刺。

items.en: Today a team can dive into a project on day one.
items.cn: 今天一支队伍可以第一天就扑进项目。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the dive sound, while the meaning group gathers other downward plunges.
note.cn: 形近组保留 dive 的音形，近义组则是几种向下的猛扎。

entries.definition: a person who works under water
the sport of entering water head first
to make a vehicle move along
to fall or push suddenly downwards
to fall or let something fall

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a body folded at the pool edge and end with a share price in free fall.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从池边折下的身体开始，落到一路下坠的股价。

normal.en: Dive and deep share an old root: to go down into something.
normal.cn: dive 与 deep 同源，都是往里面下去。

normal.en: She dived under the wave and came up laughing.
normal.cn: 她从浪下钻过去，冒出来时在笑。

normal.en: The goalkeeper dived and just touched the ball.
normal.cn: 守门员扑出去，刚好碰到球。

normal.en: He dived into the report and forgot his lunch.
normal.cn: 他一头扎进报告，连午饭都忘了。

normal.en: Sales dived in the first cold week of winter.
normal.cn: 入冬第一个冷周，销量猛跌。

abstract.en: Picture a body folding into one straight line above water.
abstract.cn: 想象身体在水面上方折成一条直线。

abstract.en: Picture a seabird closing its wings and dropping.
abstract.cn: 想象一只海鸟收翅直落。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a chart falling off the bottom edge.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上的线跌出底边。

examples.en: He dived from the top board without hesitating.
examples.cn: 他从最高跳板毫不犹豫地跳下。

examples.en: Prices dived after the report was published.
examples.cn: 报告公布后价格暴跌。

examples.en: The submarine dived to avoid the storm.
examples.cn: 潜艇下潜以避开风暴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dive 记成「往深处扎」：与 deep 同源，头朝下钻进水里是跳水，身体往下扑是俯冲，数字往下掉就是暴跌。

root: 源自古英语 dyfan（浸入、下沉），与 deep 同源，本义是往水里或深处钻。由「入水」一义发展出跳水与潜水，又由「向下」引申为俯冲、猛扑与价格急跌，并可用作名词指跳水这一动作。

sensesIntro.en: From a clean line of body above water to a chart line dropping off the page.
sensesIntro.cn: 从水面上方一条干净的身体线，到图表上跌出纸面的一条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body folded at the pool edge, falling into one straight line.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体在池边折起，落成一条直线。

branches.en: The first sense is entering water head first.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是头朝下入水。

branches.en: The second sense is any fast downward move.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是任何快速向下的移动。

branches.en: The third sense is a number falling like a diver.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是数字像跳水者一样下落。

branches.en: Both senses share one downward line.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享同一条向下的线。

branches.en: Both senses suggest speed that cannot be stopped.
branches.cn: 两个义项都暗示停不下来的速度。

intro.en: Dive belongs to an Old English family of depth words, where deep and dip stand close.
intro.cn: dive 属于古英语的「深」词一族，与 deep 和 dip 站得很近。

latinIntro.en: Old English dyfan, to dip, gives dive; the same depth root also gives deep and dip.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 dyfan（浸）给出 dive，同一个「深」的词根也给出 deep 与 dip。

items.exampleCN: 一名潜水员检查了船体。

items.meaning: the sport or work of going under
items.example: Diving is taught at the pool.
He dived and surfaced far off.
items.exampleCN: 他跳下去，在远处浮上来。

items.meaning: the American past form of dive
items.example: The bird dove at the water.
She dipped the brush in paint.
The lake is deep at the centre.

definition_zh: 精力充沛的；有力的；强健的
definition_en: full of physical strength and energy, or strong and forceful
core_image: 晨跑的人大步跨过台阶，呼吸深而稳
scene: 医生看完体检报告，说他恢复得很好，可以恢复剧烈运动了。 The doctor said he could return to vigorous exercise.
sceneCN: 这里 vigorous 是「剧烈的、有力的」（第 2 个义项：强度大而有力量）；句意为医生说他可以恢复剧烈运动了。大步跨台阶、呼吸深稳的晨跑者就是这个词给人的感觉。

pos.zh: 精力充沛的；有力的；强健的

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成名词，义为「精力；活力」（美式 vigor）
加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「有力地；精力充沛地」
加前缀 in- 与后缀 -ate 构成，义为「使振奋；使有活力」

senses.title: Full of bodily strength
senses.definition: strong, healthy, and full of energy
senses.definitionCN: 强壮、健康且充满活力
senses.example: At seventy he is still vigorous and walks five miles a day.
senses.exampleCN: 他七十岁仍精力充沛，每天走五英里。
senses.why: Latin vigor meant liveliness and force, and a vigorous person carries both.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vigor 意为活力与力量，精力充沛的人两者兼有。

senses.title: Strong in force or intensity
senses.definition: done with great force or energy
senses.definitionCN: 以很大力量或强度完成的
senses.example: The doctor said he could return to vigorous exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说他可以恢复剧烈运动了。
senses.why: The same force, applied to an activity rather than a person, makes the activity vigorous.
senses.whyCN: 同一股力量若落到活动上而非人身上，活动本身就变得有力、剧烈。

senses.title: Lively and forceful in speech or style
senses.definition: expressed with energy and confidence
senses.definitionCN: 表达得充满能量与自信
senses.example: She made a vigorous defence of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她为这项计划做了有力的辩护。
senses.why: Language borrows the body and puts its force into argument.
senses.whyCN: 语言借用身体的力量，把它注入论辩之中。

senses.title: Growing strongly
senses.definition: growing fast and healthily, as a plant does
senses.definitionCN: 像植物那样快速而健康地生长
senses.example: Vigorous growth followed the spring rain.
senses.exampleCN: 春雨之后出现了旺盛的生长。
senses.why: What is strong in body is active in growth as well.
senses.whyCN: 强健之物在生长上也同样有劲。

senses.title: Energetic in a public effort
senses.definition: carried out with much energy by a group
senses.definitionCN: 由一个群体以大量精力开展的
senses.example: The city ran a vigorous campaign against litter.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市开展了声势浩大的反乱扔垃圾运动。
senses.why: A group with vigour turns it into a movement.
senses.whyCN: 一个有活力的群体，会把它变成一场运动。

intro.en: Vigorous rests on Latin vigor, the liveliness that makes a body act.
intro.cn: vigorous 建立在拉丁语 vigor 之上，指让身体动起来的那股活劲。

items.en: Vigere meant to be lively or to flourish, and vigor was that liveliness.
items.cn: vigere 意为有生机、繁茂，vigor 即那股生机。

items.en: French vigour carried the word with the sense of strength.
items.cn: 法语 vigour 带着「力量」的含义承接此词。

items.en: English vigour named bodily force and the force of law alike.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 vigour 既指体力，也指法律的效力。

items.en: The adjective vigorous spread to exercise, argument, and growth.
items.cn: 形容词 vigorous 扩展到运动、论辩与生长。

items.en: American spelling drops the u: vigor, but keeps vigorous.
items.cn: 美式拼写去掉 u 作 vigor，但 vigorous 不变。

note.en: The first group holds the vigour family, the second the words for strength and its lack.
note.cn: 第一组是 vigour 词族，第二组是力量及其缺乏的表达。

normalIntro.en: Vigour is the noun, vigorous the adjective, and in- can hand the energy out again.
normalIntro.cn: vigour 是名词，vigorous 是形容词，加上 in- 就能把能量再分给别人。

normal.en: Vigour plus -ous gives vigorous, as if full of vigour.
normal.cn: vigour 加 -ous 得 vigorous，意为充满活力。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with rigorous, which means strict.
normal.cn: 别与 rigorous（严格的）混淆。

normal.en: American English writes vigor but still writes vigorous.
normal.cn: 美式写作 vigor，但形容词仍是 vigorous。

normal.en: Invigorate means to put vigour into someone.
normal.cn: invigorate 意为把活力注入某人。

normal.en: Latin vigere, to flourish, also hides in vigil, a night watch.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 vigere（繁茂）也藏在 vigil（守夜）里。

abstract.en: See a runner taking the steps two at a time.
abstract.cn: 想跑者一次跨两级台阶。

abstract.en: Feel a deep, steady breath after a hard climb.
abstract.cn: 感受费力爬坡后深而稳的呼吸。

abstract.en: Watch a young shoot push up fast after rain.
abstract.cn: 看雨后新芽猛地往上蹿。

examples.en: She is a vigorous campaigner for cleaner air.
examples.cn: 她是一位为更清洁空气奔走的活动家。

examples.en: The plants showed vigorous growth in warm weather.
examples.cn: 天气温暖时植株生长旺盛。

examples.en: He shook my hand in a vigorous grip.
examples.cn: 他有力地握住我的手摇了摇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威哥热死」——威哥热得满头汗还跑第一，精力不是一般的充沛。

root: 拉丁语 vigere（有生机；繁茂）→ vigor（活力）→ 法语 vigour → 英语 vigorous

sensesIntro.en: One Latin word for liveliness spreads from a strong body to strong exercise, strong speech, fast growth, and loud public action.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个表示生机的拉丁词，从强健的身体延伸到剧烈的运动、有力的言辞、旺盛的生长与声势浩大的行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner taking the steps two at a time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次跨两级台阶的跑者。

branches.en: The body branch: a strong man of seventy.
branches.cn: 身体分支：七十岁仍强健的人。

branches.en: The activity branch: back to vigorous exercise.
branches.cn: 活动分支：恢复剧烈运动。

branches.en: The speech branch: a vigorous defence of the plan.
branches.cn: 言辞分支：为计划作有力辩护。

branches.en: The plant branch: growth after spring rain.
branches.cn: 植物分支：春雨后的旺盛生长。

branches.en: The group branch: a campaign against litter.
branches.cn: 群体分支：声势浩大的反垃圾运动。

intro.en: The stem vig- means to be lively; -ous and -ly build the adjective and adverb, in- adds energy to others.
intro.cn: 词干 vig- 意为有生机，-ous、-ly 构成形容词与副词，in- 表示把能量给别人。

latinIntro.en: Latin vigere produced vigor and the English family vigorous, vigorously, and invigorate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vigere 产生 vigor，以及英语中的 vigorous、vigorously、invigorate。

items.example: Vigour is the state of being lively.
They argued vigorously for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 他们激烈辩论了一小时。

items.example: A vigil keeps watch through the night.
A feeble step next to a vigorous one.
items.exampleCN: 虚弱的步子旁边是有力的步子。

items.example: Rigorous rules are not vigorous ones.
items.exampleCN: 严格的规则不等于有力的规则。

items.example: A robust frame is a vigorous one.
items.exampleCN: 结实的体格就是强健的体格。

definition_zh: 吸毒成瘾者；对某活动上瘾的人；入迷者；酒瘾者；网络成瘾者；赌博成瘾者；有瘾的人；医学上的依赖者
definition_en: a person who cannot stop using a substance or doing an activity, or who is devoted to it almost completely
core_image: 一个人被一条看不见的绳子系在某样东西上，越挣扎系得越紧
scene: 他每天醒来第一件事就是找酒瓶，家人劝了多次也没有用。 He had become a heavy drinker, an addict who could not face a morning without alcohol.
sceneCN: 这里 addict 是「酒瘾者」（第 4 个义项：对酒精成瘾的人）；句意为他已经成了重度饮酒者，一个早上离不开酒的瘾者。

pos.zh: 名词：成瘾者；入迷的人；有瘾的人
动词：使上瘾；使沉溺（多用于 addict oneself to）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「成瘾；沉溺」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ed 构成，义为「上瘾的；沉迷的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「使人上瘾的」
由 addictive 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「成瘾性」

senses.title: A person dependent on drugs
senses.definition: a person who is physically or psychologically dependent on an illegal or controlled drug
senses.definitionCN: 对非法或受管制药物产生生理或心理依赖的人
senses.example: The clinic offers treatment for young drug addicts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所收治年轻的吸毒成瘾者。
senses.why: The core image is a rope: the drug holds the person and the person keeps returning to it.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一根绳子：药物拴住了人，人也不断回到它那里。

senses.title: A person hooked on an activity
senses.definition: a person who cannot stop doing a particular activity, such as shopping, gaming or exercise
senses.definitionCN: 无法停止某项活动的人，如购物、游戏或运动
senses.example: He is a gym addict who trains twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个健身成瘾者，一天训练两次。
senses.why: The rope need not be a substance: any repeated act can fasten itself to a life.
senses.whyCN: 绳子不一定是物质：任何重复的行为都能把自己系到一个人的生活上。

senses.title: An enthusiastic devotee
senses.definition: a person who is very enthusiastic about something and spends much time on it, without a medical sense
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物非常热情、投入大量时间的人，不含医学上的成瘾义
senses.example: She is a film addict who sees every new release.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个电影迷，每部新片都看。
senses.why: The same devotion appears here as pleasure rather than compulsion.
senses.whyCN: 同样的投入在这里显现为乐趣，而不是强迫。

senses.title: A person dependent on alcohol
senses.definition: a person who is dependent on alcohol and cannot control drinking
senses.definitionCN: 依赖酒精、无法控制饮酒的人
senses.example: The programme helps alcohol addicts rebuild their lives.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目帮助酒瘾者重建生活。
senses.why: Alcohol is one more rope, and the image of the tied person stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 酒精是又一根绳子，被系住的人的意象保持不变。

senses.title: A person addicted to the internet
senses.definition: a person whose use of the internet or screens has become compulsive and harmful
senses.definitionCN: 上网或使用屏幕已成强迫行为并造成损害的人
senses.example: Many parents worry that their child has become an internet addict.
senses.exampleCN: 许多父母担心孩子已经成了网络成瘾者。
senses.why: A new medium provides a new rope, but the knot is the same old one.
senses.whyCN: 新的媒介提供新的绳子，打的结却是同一种旧结。

senses.title: A compulsive gambler
senses.definition: a person who cannot stop gambling even when it ruins their money and relationships
senses.definitionCN: 即使赌博毁掉钱财与关系也无法停止的人
senses.example: The support group was founded by a recovered gambling addict.
senses.exampleCN: 这个互助小组由一位康复的赌博成瘾者创立。
senses.why: Chance itself becomes the rope, pulling the person back to the table.
senses.whyCN: 偶然性本身成了绳子，把人一次次拉回赌桌。

senses.title: A generic label for a person with a compulsion
senses.definition: a general noun for anyone whose dependence on something dominates their daily life, with the object left unstated
senses.definitionCN: 泛指任何对某物的依赖支配了日常生活的人，具体对象不点明
senses.example: The shelter takes in addicts of every kind, not only drug users.
senses.exampleCN: 这家收容所接收各种有瘾的人，不只是吸毒者。
senses.why: With no object named, the word keeps only the bare image of a person tied fast.
senses.whyCN: 不点明对象时，这个词只剩「人被紧紧系住」这一赤裸意象。

senses.title: A patient with a diagnosed dependency
senses.definition: in medical and clinical usage, a patient formally diagnosed with a substance or behavioural dependency
senses.definitionCN: 在医学与临床语境中，被正式诊断为物质依赖或行为依赖的患者
senses.example: The ward admits addicts for supervised withdrawal.
senses.exampleCN: 这个病房收治成瘾者进行监督下戒断。
senses.why: The rope becomes a clinical category, measured and treated rather than judged.
senses.whyCN: 绳子在这里成为临床类别，被测量与治疗，而不是被评判。

intro.en: Addict goes back to a Latin verb for assigning a person to someone, and that legal sense of being handed over survives under the modern medical one.
intro.cn: addict 可上溯到拉丁语中表示「把人判归某人」的动词，这种「被交付」的法律意味残留在现代医学义之下。

items.en: dicere meant 'to say, declare, proclaim', and it is the source of many English words in dict-.
items.cn: dicere 意为「说、宣告、宣布」，是英语中许多 dict- 词的来源。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus dicere 'declare' formed addicere, 'to assign, award, devote, surrender'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 dicere「宣告」构成 addicere，义为「判归、授予、献身、交出」。

items.en: The participle addictus meant 'assigned, devoted, bound over', often of a person given over to another or to a habit.
items.cn: 分词 addictus 意为「被判归的、献身的、交付的」，常指被交给他人或某种习性的人。

items.en: English first used the word for a person devoted to something; the modern drug sense is much later, from the twentieth century.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指「献身于某事物的人」；现代「吸毒成瘾者」义要晚得多，属二十世纪。

items.en: Medicine turned the old legal bond into a diagnosis, and everyday speech extended addict to screens, gambling, gyms and films.
items.cn: 医学把古老的法律束缚变成诊断，日常语言则把 addict 扩展到屏幕、赌博、健身与电影。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin family of addictus; the near-meaning group gathers words for dependent users and intense enthusiasts.
note.cn: 形近组收 addictus 的拉丁词族；近义组收表示依赖者与极度爱好者的一族词。

entries.definition: The noun for the condition of being dependent on a substance or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成瘾、沉溺」，指对某物质或活动的依赖状态。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning dependent on or devoted to something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「上瘾的、沉迷的」，由本词加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning likely to make someone dependent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「使人上瘾的」，由本词加 -ive 构成。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to say words for someone to write, from the same Latin dicere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「口述、命令」，与 addict 同出拉丁 dicere「说」，但前缀不同。

entries.definition: A neutral word for a person who uses a drug, often preferred in official contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「使用者」，在中立或官方语境中常用来指用药者，语气比 addict 温和。

entries.definition: A person who uses a substance harmfully, with the focus on the misuse rather than the dependence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「滥用者」，侧重有害使用而非依赖。

entries.definition: A person with strong interest in an activity, without any idea of compulsion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「爱好者、热情者」，不含强迫的意味。

entries.definition: A person who is very devoted to a person, cause or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「献身者、狂热爱好者」，强调投入与忠诚。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb for assigning a person and the modern collocations of the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁「判归某人」动词，以及这个名词的现代搭配。

normal.en: addicere is to hand a person over: an addict is someone handed over to a habit.
normal.cn: addicere 是「把人交付出去」：addict 就是被交给某种习性的人。

normal.en: dicere is to declare, which is why dictate and addict share a root.
normal.cn: dicere 是「宣告」，所以 dictate 与 addict 共有一个词根。

normal.en: The noun takes the stress on the first syllable; the verb takes it on the second.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节。

normal.en: Be addicted to is the common adjectival pattern for dependence.
normal.cn: be addicted to 是表示依赖的常见形容词结构。

normal.en: In modern use the word stretches from drugs to screens, gambling and films.
normal.cn: 现代用法把这个词从毒品扩展到屏幕、赌博与电影。

abstract.en: Picture a thin rope tied around a person's wrist and fastened to a bottle, a screen or a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细绳系在人的手腕上，另一头系在酒瓶、屏幕或赌桌上。

abstract.en: The rope does not care what it is tied to; only the pulling is the same in every case.
abstract.cn: 绳子不在乎系在什么上；每一种情形里相同的只是那股拉力。

abstract.en: Sometimes the rope is a pleasure rather than a prison, which is why a film addict is not a patient.
abstract.cn: 有时绳子是乐趣而非牢笼，所以电影迷并不算病人。

examples.en: The centre provides clean needles for drug addicts.
examples.cn: 该中心为吸毒成瘾者提供清洁针具。

examples.en: He described himself as a recovering gambling addict.
examples.cn: 他称自己是一名正在康复的赌博成瘾者。

examples.en: She was addicted to her phone and checked it every minute.
examples.cn: 她对手机上瘾，每分钟都要看一眼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿迪克特」——阿迪被一根绳子系在瓶子上，怎么挣也挣不开：成瘾者

root: 拉丁语 addicere（ad-「向」+ dicere「宣告」）意为「判归、交付、献身」，分词 addictus 指被交付给他人或某种习性的人；现代「成瘾者」义由这一「被束缚」的意象发展而来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of addict all describe a person tied to something: a drug, an activity, a hobby, alcohol, the internet, gambling, any compulsion at all, or a clinical diagnosis.
sensesIntro.cn: addict 的八个义项都在描述一个被系住的人：毒品、活动、爱好、酒精、网络、赌博、任何强迫，或一项临床诊断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with a thin rope tied to the wrist, the other end fastened to something they cannot leave.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人手腕上系着细绳，另一端系在他离不开的东西上。

branches.en: SUBSTANCES: drugs and alcohol are the oldest ropes, tied to the body itself.
branches.cn: 物质线：毒品与酒精是最古老的绳子，直接系在身体上。

branches.en: BEHAVIOURS: gyms, screens and gambling tables provide ropes made of repeated acts.
branches.cn: 行为线：健身、屏幕与赌桌提供由重复行为编成的绳子。

branches.en: ENTHUSIASM: the same devotion appears without the element of compulsion.
branches.cn: 热情线：同样的投入在这里不含强迫的成分。

branches.en: GENERIC: with no object named, only the bare image of a tied person remains.
branches.cn: 泛称线：不点明对象时，只剩「被系住的人」这一赤裸意象。

branches.en: CLINIC: the rope becomes a diagnosis, measured and treated by professionals.
branches.cn: 临床线：绳子变成诊断，由专业人员测量与治疗。

intro.en: Addict is a Latin prefix plus dicere 'declare'; Latin participles supply the noun, English suffixes the rest of the family.
intro.cn: addict 由一个拉丁前缀加 dicere「宣告」构成；拉丁分词提供名词形态，英语后缀扩展其余部分。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicere, addicere and addictus are recorded, so only the deepest Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dicere、addicere 与 addictus 均有记录，只有最深层的印欧词根属于重构。

items.example: It is the speaking root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族中「说」的词根。

items.example: The legal sense of handing over survives in the English word.
items.exampleCN: 「交付」的法律意味在英语词中留存下来。

items.meaningCN: 被判归的；献身的；被交付的
items.example: It is the direct base of addict.
items.exampleCN: 它是 addict 的直接基础。

definition_zh: 椭圆形的；卵形的；椭圆；椭圆形场地
definition_en: shaped like an egg, with no corners and two long sides, or a shape or a sports ground of that form
core_image: 一只白蛋放在木桌上，蛋壳的轮廓被晨光勾出一条柔和的线
scene: 旧货店的角落里放着一张矮桌，桌面被磨得发亮，四边没有一处直角。 The table in the corner has an oval top.
sceneCN: 这里的 oval 是「椭圆形的」（第 1 个义项：像蛋一样的圆润形状）；句意为角落里那张桌子有一个椭圆形的桌面。图中可辨识物件：矮桌、磨亮的桌面、店角的阴影。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 ov-（蛋）加希腊来源的 -oid（像……的）构成，义为「卵形的」
来自拉丁语 ovatus（卵形的），多用于植物学，义为「卵形的」
由 oval 与 shaped 复合而成，义为「椭圆形的」

senses.title: Shaped like an egg
senses.definition: having a rounded shape that is longer than it is wide, with no corners, like an egg
senses.definitionCN: 圆润、长大于宽、没有棱角，形状像一枚蛋
senses.example: The table in the corner has an oval top.
senses.exampleCN: 角落里的那张桌子有一个椭圆形的桌面。
senses.why: Oval comes from the Latin word for an egg, so the shape is named after the most familiar object that has it.
senses.whyCN: oval 来自拉丁语中表示「蛋」的词，所以这个形状是用最常见、天生带着它的事物来命名的。

senses.title: A closed shape with two long sides
senses.definition: a flat shape with no corners, longer in one direction than in the other
senses.definitionCN: 一种没有棱角的平面形状，一个方向比另一个方向长
senses.example: She drew an oval on the board and divided it in two.
senses.exampleCN: 她在板上画了一个椭圆，把它分成两半。
senses.why: Once the adjective named the shape, English used the same word as a noun for the shape itself, without adding any suffix.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个形容词已经命名了形状，英语就把同一个词直接作名词用，指形状本身，不必另加后缀。

senses.title: A ground or track of that shape
senses.definition: a sports ground or running track with an oval boundary, especially in cricket and Australian rules
senses.definitionCN: 边界呈椭圆形的运动场或跑道，尤用于板球与澳式足球
senses.example: The match was played on a small oval near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛在河边一个不大的椭圆场地上进行。
senses.why: A field bounded by that curve takes its name from the curve, which is why a cricket ground is simply called an oval.
senses.whyCN: 以这条曲线为边界的场地就借这条曲线得名，所以板球场干脆就叫「椭圆」。

intro.en: Oval comes from Latin ovum, an egg, through the adjective ovalis; English borrowed it from French in the seventeenth century and now uses it for the shape, the outline and the ground.
intro.cn: oval 来自拉丁语 ovum（蛋），经形容词 ovalis 而来；英语十七世纪从法语借入，如今用来指这种形状、这条轮廓以及这种场地。

items.en: Ovum was the ordinary Latin word for an egg, and it supplied the stem ov- for everything egg-shaped.
items.cn: ovum 是拉丁语中表示「蛋」的常用词，为一切与蛋形有关的事物提供了词干 ov-。

items.en: Ovatus meant egg-shaped, and Roman writers used it for anything with that kind of outline.
items.cn: ovatus 意为卵形的，罗马作家用它形容具有那种轮廓的东西。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed ovalis, an adjective built on ovum with the ending -alis, meaning belonging to.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语造出形容词 ovalis，由 ovum 加表示「属于……」的 -alis 构成。

items.en: French passed the adjective on as oval, and English adopted it in the seventeenth century for the curved outline itself.
items.cn: 法语把这一形容词作 oval 传出，英语在十七世纪借入，用来指这条弯曲的轮廓本身。

items.en: Modern English uses oval as an adjective, as a noun for the shape, and as a name for grounds bounded by that curve.
items.cn: 现代英语让 oval 兼作形容词、指形状的名词，以及以这条曲线为界的场地之名。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin stem for egg; the near-meaning group collects words for rounded and elongated shapes.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「蛋」词干上的词；近义组收表示圆润、拉长的形状的词。

entries.definition: Shaped like an egg, especially in three dimensions.
entries.definitionCN: 形状像蛋的，尤指立体的。

entries.definition: Egg-shaped, a term used mostly in botany.
entries.definitionCN: 卵形的，主要用于植物学。

entries.definition: The organ in which eggs are produced.
A female reproductive cell; an egg.
Shaped like a regular oval with two fixed points.
entries.definitionCN: 具有两个定点的规则椭圆形的。

entries.definition: Having the form of an egg, wider at one end.
entries.definitionCN: 具有蛋的形状，一端较宽。

entries.definition: Longer than wide but with four right-angled corners.
entries.definitionCN: 长大于宽但四角为直角的；长方形的。

entries.definition: Shaped like a circle or a ball, with no long axis.
entries.definitionCN: 圆形的或球形的，没有长轴。

normalIntro.en: Oval is an adjective grown from the Latin word for an egg, so its hooks go back to a kitchen object rather than to geometry.
normalIntro.cn: oval 是从拉丁语「蛋」长出来的形容词，所以记忆钩子回到一件厨房里的东西，而不是几何学。

normal.en: Oval starts from the Latin ovum, an egg, so the word literally means egg-shaped.
normal.cn: oval 从拉丁语 ovum（蛋）出发，字面上就是「蛋形的」。

normal.en: The same ov- stem gives ovary and ovum, which belong to the biology of eggs.
normal.cn: 同一个 ov- 词干还给出 ovary 与 ovum，都属于与卵有关的生物学。

normal.en: The famous office in the White House takes its name from the curved walls of that room, not from any egg.
normal.cn: 白宫那间著名的办公室得名于房间弯曲的墙，而不是因为任何一只蛋。

normal.en: Oval and circle differ in one point: an oval is stretched, so it has two long sides instead of one even radius.
normal.cn: oval 与 circle 只差一点：椭圆被拉长了，所以它有两条长边，而不是处处半径相等。

normal.en: The ending -al turns a Latin stem into an adjective, as it does in normal and final.
normal.cn: 词尾 -al 把拉丁词干变成形容词，normal 与 final 也是如此。

abstract.en: A shape named after an egg suggests that geometry begins with things the hand already knows.
abstract.cn: 一个以蛋命名的形状说明：几何学是从手已经熟悉的东西开始的。

abstract.en: An oval has no corners, so it guides movement round instead of stopping it, which is why tracks are built in that shape.
abstract.cn: 椭圆没有棱角，所以它引导移动绕行而不是停下，跑道建成这个形状正是为此。

abstract.en: Naming a shape after the most ordinary object is a small admission that language grows out of the kitchen before it reaches the classroom.
abstract.cn: 用最平常的物件给形状命名，是承认语言先在厨房里长出来，之后才走进教室。

examples.en: The table in the corner has an oval top.
examples.cn: 角落里的那张桌子有一个椭圆形的桌面。

examples.en: She drew an oval on the board and divided it in two.
examples.cn: 她在板上画了一个椭圆，把它分成两半。

examples.en: The match was played on a small oval near the river.
examples.cn: 比赛在河边一个不大的椭圆场地上进行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃」——欧沃手里捧着一只蛋，蛋的轮廓就是椭圆；记住 oval 是椭圆形的。

root: 来自中世纪拉丁语 ovalis（卵形的），再上溯拉丁语 ovum（蛋），十七世纪经法语进入英语；同族词多与「卵、蛋形」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the outline of an egg; the senses divide into the adjective for that shape, the noun for the curve itself, and the ground bounded by it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一枚蛋的轮廓；义项按「形容这种形状的形容词」「指这条曲线本身的名词」「以它为界的场地」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white egg on a wooden table, its outline traced by the morning light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只白蛋放在木桌上，蛋壳的轮廓被晨光勾出一条柔和的线。

branches.en: a table top worn smooth at the edges
branches.cn: 边缘被磨得光滑的一张桌面

branches.en: a line chalked on a board and split in half
branches.cn: 在黑板上画出又被分成两半的一条线

branches.en: a field ringed by a low fence
branches.cn: 被一道矮栏围住的场地

branches.en: the shape in a table and the shape on a board
branches.cn: 桌面上的形状与板上的形状

branches.en: a curve that names both a figure and a field
branches.cn: 一条既命名图形又命名场地的曲线

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of belonging built on the noun for egg, passed through French and used in English for a shape, a figure and a ground.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在「蛋」这个名词上的拉丁语形容词，表示归属，经法语传入英语，用来指形状、图形与场地。

latinIntro.en: Latin ovum, ovatus and medieval Latin ovalis are all recorded, so this family has a reliable Latin ancestry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ovum、ovatus 与中世纪拉丁语 ovalis 均有记录，因此这一族词有可靠的拉丁语世系。
